title: ValeHealth on-prem implementation capture
content:
Call notes (2024-09-17) — discovery with ValeHealth (CTO: Aaron Li, SecOps: Maya Singh, Arch: Dan Ochoa)

- Context: ValeHealth is a mid-sized digital health provider planning to run conversational triage + discharge-summary generation inside their data center (air-gapped option discussed). They must not send PHI outside their network. Primary asks: private control plane with VPC peering to their corp network, KMS/HSM integration for key material, audit logs for every inference, and 12 month retention for audit records.

- Key constraints called out by customer:
  - PHI: full PHI scope, must meet SOC2 + HIPAA controls.
  - Network: strict egress rules; anything that talks to hosted control plane needs explicit allow list.
  - Hardware: they will provision 2x A100 80GB per zone initially, plan to add 4x after pilot.
  - Throughput target: 12 concurrent triage sessions, average 40 tokens/response, target p95 token latency per token <= 90ms (end-to-end p95 for a 200-token response <= 18s) — customer expects interactive feel.
  - Burst behavior: expect spikes morning 8–10AM and post-op 3–5PM.

- Functional reqs (high level):
  1) On-prem Redwood Private with local model hosting and local KV/prefix caching.
  2) VPC-only control plane connectivity (can run in their VPC or peered) — no public IPs on inference nodes.
  3) KMS or HSM integration: must support AWS CloudHSM or on-prem Thales via KMIP.
  4) Audit logs: immutable tamper-evident logs for each request (user id, route, token counts, prompt hash).
  5) Structured outputs: discharge summary templates + JSON schema enforcement + function-calling hooks.
  6) Streaming WebSocket support for triage chat UI.
  7) Canary deploys and fast rollback; cannot have model drift affecting PHI fidelity.

- Non-functional / ops notes:
  - Warmup: with A100s expect ~20–40s cold start for large Llama-family models to reach peak throughput. Need pre-warm policy for scheduled windows.
  - Batch sizing: small batch sizes to preserve latency SLO; recommend continuous batching with low-latency cutoff (15ms).
  - KV cache: prefix caching will significantly cut token generation for repetitive triage prompts; plan to instrument cache hit rate in pilot.
  - Quantization: they want FP16 or 4-bit quant for cost; warn: 4-bit may slightly degrade token-level probabilities -> risks for hallucination in medical text. We should plan eval prompts + acceptance criteria.
  - Telemetry: customer wants token-level cost/latency breakdown exported to Splunk (on-prem) every 1 minute.

- Gotchas / open technical risks:
  - Network egress policy: Control plane components that check for model updates may require egress. Customer requires whitelisting; need to enumerate IPs and acceptable update cadence. Offline update flow (airgap) must be documented.
  - HSM cert exchange: support for KMIP versions and cert rotation timeline — Ops needs runbook for emergency rotation.
  - Model licensing: some open models require attribution; legal to confirm whether ValeHealth agrees to the model license and distribution in-country.
  - Tokenization mismatch: current front-end uses older tokenizer library; we need to validate prompt/encoding parity to avoid token count surprises and cost overruns.
  - Long output trimming: discharge summaries sometimes exceed 1,000 tokens; need to support streaming + progressive flush to UI and chunked audit records.

- Example acceptance tests ValeHealth suggested (rough):
  1) PHI redaction test: send synthetic PHI and ensure logs do not contain raw PHI in plaintext except authorized fields.
  2) Latency test: 200-token generation p50 < 2s, p95 < 18s under steady load of 12 concurrent sessions.
  3) Regression test: standard eval suite of 150 prompts for hallucination / clinical accuracy; failure rate < 3% vs baseline model.

- Quick numbers back-of-envelope (for sizing discussion):
  - If we run Llama-3-classic-70B FP16 on A100-80: single GPU peak concurrency for low-latency ~6–8 simultaneous single-stream sessions (depends on context length). With 2 GPUs expect ~12–16 sessions — matches their initial 12 target.
  - If they quantize to 4-bit, can increase concurrency ~1.5x but verify regressions.

- Prompts / eval plan notes to self:
  - Set up a small eval harness with their sample chart notes (deidentified) + golden summaries from clinicians. Use rouge/med-sa metrics and human spot checks.
  - Create prompt templates that force structured JSON output with explicit "extractionConfidence" fields so UI can flag low-confidence sections for clinician review.

- Compliance & legal items to loop in:
  - Legal: confirm data residency policies and model license acceptability.
  - Security: run threat model for Private control plane; provide pen-test window.
  - Privacy: document data retention and deletion for audit logs (they asked 12 months but want ability to purge per request).

- Action items / next steps (owners + dates):
  - Priya: Draft on-prem architecture sketch & airgap flow; include IP whitelist and update cadence -> due 2024-09-23.
  - Jordan: Prep rough cost/throughput matrix comparing FP16 vs 4-bit and likely concurrency -> due 2024-09-25.
  - Evan: Prototype tokenizer parity check using ValeHealth frontend sample prompts; report tokenization deltas -> due 2024-09-26.
  - Rita: Open legal thread with licensing & PHI handling questions; sync with Legal -> create ticket VALE-124 by 2024-09-20.
  - Schedule: Book follow-up workshop for pilot scoping (architect deep-dive + security) w/ ValeHealth and infra ops -> target week of 2024-09-30.

- Meeting artifacts to attach to pilot folder (TODO):
  - Synthetic PHI test vectors (anonymized)
  - Clinician gold-summaries (deid) for eval harness
  - Network diagrams and firewall rules template for their infra team

- Notes to self (raw):
  - Keep canary window small, ensure rollback by model tag (do not rely on in-place weights swap without versioned checkpoints).
  - Need a short (1–2 slide) cheat sheet on expected latency/cold-start behavior for sales to set expectations.
  - Consider offering a Managed Updates opt-in where we push vetted model/security updates on a monthly cadence to reduce their ops burden.

- Questions to raise in next call:
  1) Can ValeHealth provide a stable internal registry (S3 or Artifactory) for model artifacts and container images?
  2) Which exact HSM vendors do they have on-prem? (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Gemalto?)
  3) Do they expect encryption-in-use (SGX/Confidential VMs) beyond KMS-at-rest?

End of raw capture.

-- Priya (notes kept informal, will formalize into pilot scoping doc after internal sync)
